inn_guide_start_text: 1. Raise the Frithstone. It is in the hammer's Misc tab. Where it burns, the frith holds - and Hugin comes down to explain the rest, a piece at a time as the settlement grows. 2. Wall it in. A frith is an enclosure. The settlement's inside and outside follow the walls you build, and so do your people: they shelter behind the wall and defend it. Leave a gate. 3. Take people in. Bring coins to the stone and recruit from this panel. Each resident costs more than the last; the Settings tab shows the price of the next one. 4. A bed each, and chests. Every resident needs a bed of their own inside the walls. Residents store what they bring home in the settlement's chests and eat from them, so put chests up early. 5. Hand out crafts on the Settlers tab. A resident with no craft does nothing useful.
inn_guide_crafts_text: Lumberjack - fells trees, clears logs and stumps, hauls the wood home. Can be set to replant instead. Forager - berries, mushrooms, thistle and seeds. Hunter - hunts the animals you allow and brings back meat and hides. Leaves tamed animals, bosses and raid creatures alone. Fisherman - takes a boat out, fishes and brings the catch home. Needs a rod and a boat moored at the settlement. Cook - takes raw food from the chests, cooks it at the stations and stores what comes off. Caretaker - the household: sorts the chests, picks up what is lying about, feeds fires and furnaces. See its own page. Farmer - sows, tends and harvests the fields you stake out. See Fields. Builder - mends damaged buildings and raises plans laid with the Builder's Hammer. Guard - watches the ground around the stone, walks the patrol points you plant (standing torches) and answers attacks. Follower - leaves the settlement to travel with you. See Followers. Smith - makes things at the settlement's crafting stations from what is in the chests, up to the targets on the Stock tab, from the recipes the founder has learned. Before that it mends: residents hand broken tools in at a chest while there is a Smith, and it takes them out, mends them and puts them back. And it keeps arrows in the chests for every resident with a bow (setting: ArrowsPerArcher): flint arrows, unless the setting SmithArrow names another kind. Miner - greyed out until it has been watched through a full session. The setting Work/OfferUnfinishedCrafts hands it out anyway. A resident gets better at the craft it works: faster swings, more from a tree or a rock.
inn_guide_panel_text: Use the Frithstone to open it. Settlers - every craft, everyone holding it, and what each is doing right now. Press a name to open that resident: mood and its reasons, health, pack and gear, trait and skills, craft, weapon preference, work area and chest. You can rename them, change how they look, send them to another stone or dismiss them. Stock - what the settlement has and how much of each thing it wants. Set a target and residents work up to it and stop; food under its target is not eaten. Construction - the plans laid for the Builder and how far along each is. Trade - the settlement's name, roads to your other settlements, the work party and the caravans. Household - who may give orders here. A Leader has the founder's authority except over naming Leaders and handing on the stone. Anyone else is a visitor: they can look and change nothing, and cannot strike your residents. Settings - work reach, needs, panel size and more. "All settings" opens every setting the mod has - so does the Innangard button in the game's pause menu. Server-side settings are admin only.
inn_guide_areas_text: Work areas are drawn on the world map. Allowed areas are yellow circles, forbidden areas red, each with its own size and the crafts it is for - so a small hunting ground and a wide felling site can sit side by side, and the bog in the middle can be kept out. Only explored ground can be drawn on. Open the map editor from the Settings tab. Trees, ore, bushes, game and the residents themselves show on the map. Inside and outside. The settlement's shape comes from what you have built. Residents stand inside the walls to use what is inside them, and will walk round to the gate rather than reach over the palisade. Keep-out circles also cut pieces out of fields, which is how a field gets a shape that is not a circle.
inn_guide_chests_text: What a chest is for. Shift+$KEY_Use on a chest opens its sorting window: - Kinds - meat, food, metal, materials, trophies and so on. Press as many as you like. - Whatever it already holds - the chest takes more of what it has most of: anything it holds more than one stack of, or as many stacks as of anything else. This is worked out from the contents every time, so it changes as the contents change. An empty chest takes anything. - A list I choose - exactly these things. Opened from a chest on "whatever it holds", the list starts as what is inside. - Whatever no other chest wants - the odds and ends: anything no other chest asks for comes here rather than into the first empty chest, and anything another chest does ask for is carried there. - Take everything away - nothing belongs here: empty your pockets into it and a caretaker carries everything off. - Make this chest mine alone - the settlement never touches it. The firmest claim wins. A hand-picked list beats a kind, a kind beats "Everything else", that beats a guess from the contents, that beats the odds-and-ends chest, and an empty chest comes last. Things are only ever moved to a firmer chest, so two equal chests never trade things back and forth. Reading a chest. Look at one and the line under it says what it is for - "For: Stone, Wood ... (+3)", "Takes more of: Honey", "Empty - takes anything" - and "(full)" when it is. Give a chest a name at the top of its window and the name is shown instead, and as the title of the chest window. From the chest window itself: - Keep what's inside here adds everything inside to the chest's list. - Shift+right-click on a thing pins that kind of thing to the chest, or lets it go. Letting the last one go puts the chest back to "whatever it holds". - On a chest that was told what it is for, a green frame marks what belongs and a red one what a caretaker will carry away. - Every item's tooltip ends with where it belongs in this settlement. Copy and paste. "Copy what it is for" in one chest's window, then "Paste" in the next - the rule is carried, not the name. Crafts ticked for a chest bring their day's work there and look there first. It locks nobody out. Building draws on chests. Inside the settlement, what its chests hold counts towards what you build. There is a switch for it in Settings.
inn_guide_caretaker_text: The caretaker keeps the settlement's things where they belong. What comes first. 1. Sorting the chests, picking things up off the floor, and taking what it picked up to a chest. 2. Then fires and furnaces. They may be fed a little late - but never left for more than about five minutes, and the fires get a round every morning. Rounds. Rather than walk out and back for every stray, a caretaker empties several chests before it delivers - up to six. If something else is waiting (a thing on the floor, a fire running low) it stops collecting after about 45 seconds and delivers what it has. A chest it cannot reach is skipped for a minute and the rest of the round goes on. Strays first. A chest that was told what it holds gives up everything else, and those are cleared before anything else is sorted. Drawers. With the Item Drawers mod installed, a caretaker also files things into the drawer that holds them. Gear. Residents fetch better armour, weapons and tools from the chests and put what they replaced back - the best of each kind is kept, and a hunter's bow is never the "old" version of its sword. When it looks stuck, "inn.chests" in the console lists every chest and its rule, and "inn.reach" (after "inn.debug on", looking at a chest) says whether residents can stand somewhere and use it.
inn_guide_fields_text: Stake a field with a Farm Marker (the hammer's Innangard tab). In its window say what grows there and how far the field reaches; the edge is drawn on the ground while the window is open. A field takes a crop and its own seed in turn, so it makes its own seed and never asks the settlement for more. A crop is offered only when its seed is in the settlement's chests and the biome will grow it. Where two fields overlap, the ground goes to the nearer stake; keep-out circles on the map cut pieces out. The Farmer does not hoe. It plants only on ground that is already cultivated. Hoe the field yourself with the Cultivator, and the Farmer sows it, tends it, harvests it, gathers what falls and replants. Grass inside the circle stays grass. The Farmer needs a Cultivator in its pack to plant; a harvest-only farmer works without one. Stock targets on the Stock tab stop it planting more of what the settlement has enough of.
inn_guide_life_text: Residents sleep at night, eat breakfast and supper from the chests, sit down to eat when there is a seat, and talk to each other when idle. Happiness runs from 0 to 100 and the resident's page says why: slept well, missed supper, no bed, the walls were broken, a friend was lost. A resident left unhappy long enough walks out, with a warning first. That can be turned off in Settings. Traits. Everyone comes with one of eight: Hardy, Brave, Timid, Diligent, Sluggard, Gluttonous, Sociable, Solitary. Skills. Residents get better at their craft, and at fighting - a timed block is something a new resident cannot do and a veteran usually can. After a meal a resident puts its pack down in the chests before going back to work.
inn_guide_defence_text: Guards answer whatever comes within their reach and do not chase far. The alarm can be sounded from the panel and sounds itself when a raid begins. The fight is the guards' until one falls; then everyone who can hold a weapon defends their own ground. The wounded fall back and return when healed. Nobody unarmed runs at an enemy. After a raid the loot is gathered in. Rounds. Patrol posts are standing torches put down with the hammer. On a guard's own page you choose which posts it walks and in what order; the round is a loop, and the map draws it with arrows. A resident who dies returns to the stone after a while and goes to fetch its gear from its grave.
inn_guide_followers_text:
A Follower is yours rather than the settlement's. Shift+$KEY_Use on one to tell it to follow or wait. It has three stances - Defensive, Aggressive, Passive - fights beside you, boards ships, goes through portals and into dungeons.

Followers need no sleep and eat from their own pack. Their pack is yours: the settlement never empties it into its chests.

A follower left behind somewhere in the world is sent home with "inn.follower.home" in the console.
inn_guide_builder_text: The Builder's Hammer has its own build menu, one entry per blueprint. Lay a plan and the Builder raises it from the ground up, paying each piece's full cost from the site before it goes up. A three-bed cabin comes with the mod. Writing your own. Hold the Builder's Hammer, look at a building and press B. Name it, and it is saved to BepInEx/config/Innangard/blueprints and offered by the hammer at once. Whatever is joined to the piece under your crosshair comes with it. Console: "inn.bp.capture [radius]" captures by radius, "inn.bp.place " lays one, "inn.bp.mend" re-plans whatever is missing from the building you stand in. The mod can also read a PlanBuild blueprint library you already have. The Builder also mends damaged buildings in the settlement.
inn_guide_roads_text: Two settlements of your own can be joined by a road, and caravans can run on it. Survey a way from the Trade tab. The line keeps off water, out of the mountains and off anything too steep, and leaves by your gate. Surveying builds nothing: it draws the line on the map and on the ground near you. Build it. Hoe along the line and the stretch turns green; lay it in stone and it turns pale blue. A built road carries much more than a bare line. Work party. Muster two or three residents to walk out with you; they lay what you lay where they stand and clear trees, stumps and boulders on the line. Guards and cooks stay home. Caravans. Put a trade chest at each end, fill one and press send. The carriers walk the road at the pace it allows, whether or not you are there to watch, and the goods arrive in the far trade chest. Nothing is bought or sold - both villages are yours.
inn_guide_keys_text: Keys - Shift+$KEY_Use on a chest - what the chest is for. - Shift+$KEY_Use on a follower - follow or wait. - Shift+right-click on a thing in a chest - pin it to the chest, or let it go. - B, holding the Builder's Hammer - save the building you look at as a blueprint. The Shift key can be changed in Settings, under all settings. Console (F5) - inn.chests - every chest the settlement can use, its rule and how full it is. - inn.debug on - unlocks the three test commands below for this session. - inn.reach [resident] - look at a chest: can residents stand somewhere and use it, and if not, why. - inn.selftest - checks the chest rules, names, pins and copy/paste here, and puts everything back. - inn.test.caretaker - (devcommands) sets up chests and things to sort beside you and reports how the caretakers did. - inn.overlay [on|off] - each nearby resident's craft and what it is doing, over its head. - inn.footprint [on|off] - what each settlement covers, on the map. - inn.ground - what the mod sees under your feet: road, path or bare ground. - inn.follower.home - send followers left in the world back to the stone. - inn.frith.adopt [radius] - residents whose stone is gone join the one nearest you. - inn.world.backups - the copies of this world kept before each session.
inn_guide_world_text: Never launch this world without the mod. Valheim deletes what it does not recognise, so one session without Innangard erases every stone and every resident. The mod keeps copies of the world before and after each session; "inn.world.backups" lists them. A lost stone. Raise a new Frithstone and run "inn.frith.adopt" beside it: residents nearby whose own stone is gone join it. Servers. Everyone needs the same version of the mod, down to the patch number. Settings live in BepInEx/config/com.yololo.innangard.cfg; most are also on the Settings tab. Texts are in lang/English.json beside the mod - drop another language file in that folder to translate it.

inn_lore_stone_text:
So. You have raised a Frithstone. Mark this before anything else: a frith is an enclosure. Raise walls around the stone and a gate to pass them, for what lies within the wall is yours and ordered, and what lies without is the wild. Your people will treat the wall as the edge of their world - they shelter behind it, and they defend it.

Only then bring coin to the stone and take someone in. A stone with no wall is a fire in the open, and the open belongs to the greydwarves.
inn_lore_recruit_text:
A stranger sits at your fire now. Give them a bed of their own within the walls, and chests to keep what they gather - they eat from those chests, and a hungry worker is a poor one.

Use the stone and you will find them there, waiting for a craft: the axe, the rod, the bow, or the watch. A village is made of small things, done every day.
inn_lore_trade_text:
You have given them work. Now give them ground. On the map you may draw the circles they may work in, and the ones they must keep out of. Plant patrol points, and a guard will walk between them.

What you do not draw, they will decide for themselves - and they are not always wise.
inn_lore_watch_text:
The night has teeth. Hear me: the settlement's fight belongs to the guards. The cook, the woodcutter and the fisher keep to their work and out of the way, as they should.

Only if a guard falls does the frith break, and then every hand that can hold a blade defends its own ground. So arm your guards well, and give them a bed near the wall.
inn_lore_broken_text:
A guard has fallen on watch, and the peace with them. Until the attack is over, every resident who can fight will stand on the ground they work.

When the last foe is gone the frith mends itself. The fallen return to the stone in time, and go looking for what they left in their grave. Do not bury what you need.
inn_lore_mood_text:
A hall is not held by its walls. Your people need a bed of their own under a roof, food in a chest they are allowed to take from, and a wall that stands - and whichever of those you fail to give them shows in their face at the end of the day.

The stone will tell you which it was: slept badly, missed supper, no bed at all, a friend lost. Mend it and the reckoning goes back to nothing. Leave it, and one morning you will look for them and find them gone. They will have warned you first.
inn_lore_store_text:
They will carry wood until the wood is gone, if nobody ever says otherwise. Set what the settlement wants of a thing and they will work up to that and stop - and what is held below its mark is not eaten, so a store you are keeping stays kept.

Ask for nothing and they will judge it themselves. They are willing. They are not thrifty.
inn_lore_chest_text:
Every chest within the walls belongs to the settlement. Hold shift and use one and you may say what it is for: which crafts draw their supplies from it, and what it should hold - the metal here, the meal there. The caretaker keeps to what you say and carries off whatever does not belong.

And what they hold is yours as well. Stand inside your own walls and build, and the chests answer for the cost without your opening a single one of them.
inn_lore_boat_text:
A fisherman cannot make what it fishes with. Put a rod in a chest they are allowed to draw from, and moor a boat near the stone in water deep enough to float it - a hull dragged up onto a beach is no use to anybody, and they will stand there telling you they have no boat while it sits in the sand behind them.

From the day they take it out it is the settlement's boat. Should the sea walk it off while nobody is aboard, it will be found and brought back to its mooring. Take the helm yourself and it is yours again, and it goes where you go.
inn_lore_plan_text:
A builder does not invent. Show it what to make: take up the builder's hammer, look at something you have already raised, and press the key to write it down. It is a plan from that moment - no reloading, no waiting.

Set a plan on the ground and it stands as a ghost until the builder has paid for every piece of it out of the settlement's chests. Mending is its other half: it walks your walls and makes good what the night broke.
inn_lore_free_topic: One who walks out with you
inn_lore_free_text:
This one is not the settlement's. It is yours. It will leave the wall behind, cross water with you, go through a portal and down into the dark, and it needs no bed and eats out of its own pack.

Hold shift and use them to say come or wait. Three tempers to choose between - stand and guard, go and hunt, or keep their hands down - and choose with care: the passive will not save you, and the eager will find you a fight you did not want.
inn_lore_way_text:
Two hearths, and nothing but wild between. You have asked where a road could run, and I have walked it for you: off the water, out of the mountains, round anything a laden traveller would turn an ankle on. It is a line, nothing more. No stone has been turned.

Follow it with a hoe. What you lay, I will count.
inn_lore_road_text:
There. A stretch of it is made, and it has gone green on your map - that is the ground answering, not me. Lay it in stone and it pales further, and a laden traveller walks quicker on stone than on packed earth.

Take your people out with you and it goes three times as fast. They will fell what stands in the way and go back to their crafts when you are done with them. And mark what the road is worth: over a bare line your goods go on backs and little of it goes at all. A road made end to end carries six times as much.
inn_lore_dock_text:
A chest for what leaves and what comes. Nobody here will touch it: not the caretaker who tidies everything else, not the hungry, not you when you build. What you set in it is what the next caravan carries, and what one brings is waiting in it.

Raise one at the far end too. A load must have somewhere to be set down, or it does not go.
inn_lore_cart_text:
They have gone. Two or three of your own, walking at the pace the road allows - and it allows what you built into it.

Do not wait on them. They keep walking whether you watch or sleep, and they will find the other hearth without you. Go and meet them on the way if you like the look of it. Nothing is bought and nothing sold: both halls are yours, and this is carrying, not trade.
inn_lore_field_text:
A field is not fenced. It is staked. Drive a Farm Marker into good ground and use it, and use it again, until it names a crop you have seed for and this ground will grow. Hold shift and use it to say how far the field reaches; I will draw the edge on the earth while you look.

The field takes a crop and its own seed turn about, so it feeds itself and never asks for more. A circle you forbid on the map cuts a piece back out of it. And tell the farmer how much is enough. Left to itself it will sow until the world is turnips.
inn_lore_hunt_text:
A hunter takes what you allow and nothing more. Ask at the stone which beasts are theirs to kill. The tamed, the great ones and whatever a raid brings are never theirs, whatever you say - and a beast you have led inside your walls to tame is safe there too. Out in the woods it is meat again.

Put a bow and arrows in the chests. They come home when the pack is heavy or the light goes. The rest is patience - theirs and yours.
inn_lore_felling_text:
An axe needs no lesson. But it does not know which tree you love. Look at one, hold ctrl and use it, and it will stand however the forest around it falls. Do it again and it is timber like the rest.

On their page you may turn the axe to the other work: instead of felling, they walk the ground and put back the seed you allow. A wood that is only ever cut is a wood that ends.
inn_lore_guard_text:
A guard walks. Plant patrol points and they go round them - or give one guard a round of their own, and the hours they keep it. Off watch they rest, unless the frith breaks. Then nobody is off watch.

You need not wait for the wild to sound the alarm: call them to arms from the stone, and stand them down after. And should one of yours be killed out at their work, they will come home and say where. The guards will go and look. So would I.
inn_lore_mark_text:
They have chosen a bed - the nearest to the stone, because nobody told them otherwise. If you built them a house, tell them: hold ctrl and use the resident, then the bed, and it is theirs.

The same hand says other things. Ctrl and use a tree and it stays standing. Ctrl and use a fire, a bench or a smelter and the settlement leaves it alone - the campfire you lit on the road, the second furnace you wanted cold. Do it again and it is theirs to work.
inn_lore_kin_text:
Look closely at this one. Each comes to you with a nature they will not lose - hardy or timid, brave or idle, a glutton, a talker, one who keeps to themselves - and it leans on everything they do. The page says which, and what it costs you.

The rest they learn by doing. The axe swings faster, the tree gives more, and one who took every blow on the shield learns, in time, to time it. A new hand hits like a new hand. Do not send them at a troll.
inn_lore_table_text:
Did you see that face? Every one of them likes one food above the rest, and nobody knows which until they have eaten it. Now the stone knows, and their page says it. Keep it in the chests and it will lift them more than any other meal.

They eat better sitting than standing, and better in company than alone. Put benches in the hall, a fire under a roof, and tools and armour where they can reach them. It costs you little, and they remember it.
inn_lore_household_text:
Someone else stands inside your walls. Unless this world is ruled otherwise, they may walk through and look, and change nothing - not a craft, not a chest - and they may not raise a hand to your people.

If you would share the burden, the Household page at the stone names Leaders. A Leader commands as you do, in all but two things: making other Leaders, and handing the stone on. Those stay with the one who raised it.
inn_lore_hearth_text:
A second fire. Each stone is its own frith: its own walls, its own people, its own chests, and what one holds the other does not.

But the people are yours, not the stone's. Open one's page and you may send them to the other. They go with what they carry and nothing else - bed, chest, round and fields stay behind. And when you want the two to share what they make, ask at the stone for a way between them. I know the ground.
inn_tend_transfer_desc: Bed, chest, patrol route and fields all stay behind. The resident arrives at the Frithstone you choose with nothing but what it carries.
inn_tend_transfer_none: You have raised no other Frithstone in this world.
inn_doing_new_stone: Finding its feet at a new Frithstone
inn_tend_role_not_offered: Greyed crafts are not ready yet and cannot be given out.
inn_tend_appearance_desc: Built from Valheim's own character parts. What you choose is kept, shared with everyone in the world, and survives a death.
inn_look_name_in_use: Somebody in this settlement already answers to that.
inn_tend_follower_desc: Shift and Use tells a resident to come along or to stay put, and any player may do it. Each follower keeps its own place in the line. They feed themselves from what they carry and never need a bed.
inn_alongside_combat_defensive_desc: Fights what comes at it or at the one it follows, and nothing else.
inn_alongside_combat_aggressive_desc: Goes after anything hostile within thirty metres.
inn_alongside_combat_passive_desc: Will not fight. Follows, or waits where it was told.
inn_tend_pick_the_chest_note: Ctrl and Use on the chest itself, then choose “Use as intake chest”.
inn_tend_may_hunt_note: Tamed beasts, bosses and raid creatures are never touched, whatever is ticked here.
inn_tend_weapon_hint: Bow first, then blade opens at distance and changes hands once something has closed. A resident carrying only one of the two uses that.
inn_tend_lumber_mode_hint: Felling clears trees, logs and stumps. Sowing puts allowed seeds back across the work area.
inn_tillage_fields_none: No Farm Marker reaches this Frithstone.
inn_tend_farmer_targets_hint: Leave at zero and the Farmer sows as long as there is ground. Set a number and it stops there, counting what is stored and what is still ripening in the field.
inn_tillage_target_unlimited: As much as there is ground for
inn_tend_dismiss_desc: A resident cannot be sent away carrying anything. Their bed and their chest go back to the settlement.
inn_panel_recruit_ladder: Each in turn: {0}, then the last figure for everyone after.
inn_panel_recruit_desc: The ladder is Recruitment/CostMultipliers in the config file, times Recruitment/Coins.
inn_panel_ui_scale_desc: Scales these panels and their text. Valheim's own UI scale cannot reach them, so this is the setting to raise on a large or high resolution screen. Applies to this client only.
inn_tend_craft_from_chests_desc: While you are standing in the settlement, what its chests hold counts towards what you are building, the same chests the Caretaker works out of. Turn it off if another mod already builds from containers - two of them fetching for one build is one fetch too many. This client only.
inn_area_map_open: Place areas on the world map
inn_area_map_help: Hold Ctrl and click the map to place an area. Ctrl and right-click removes the one under the cursor. This is the game's own map, so zoom and pan as usual. Your fields are drawn here too, so a keep-out circle can be laid over the part of one you do not want farmed.
inn_area_full: This frith already has as many work areas as it can hold.
inn_wayin_editor_desc: Select the perimeter doors or gates residents should prefer when entering or leaving the frith. Interior doors remain available for houses, beds and indoor storage.
inn_tend_talk_when_idle: Talking when there is no work
inn_tend_how_often_they_talk: How often they stop to talk (%)
inn_tend_patrol_radius: How wide a patrol point reaches
inn_tend_marker_reach: How far a marker may sit
inn_round_per_guard_hint: Pick a guard under Residents to give them a route of their own.
inn_round_editor_desc: Click the points in the order you want them walked. Click one again to drop it. Drag to move the map, wheel to zoom.
inn_watch_schedule_desc: Off duty, the guard rests seated by day and sleeps at night. A broken frith always puts them on duty.
inn_sendaway_still_carrying: Take everything out of their pack first.
inn_because_no_bed: Nowhere of its own to sleep
inn_because_bed_in_open: Its bed has no roof or walls round it - it wants a house
inn_because_crowded_house: Too many sleeping in one house (more than four)
inn_because_good_workshop: Its stations all in one place, under one roof
inn_because_scattered_workshop: Its stations are scattered or out in the weather - it wants them together in one building
inn_because_rich_meal: Ate a hearty dish of many things
inn_reason_held: The frith was broken and held
inn_reason_meal_interrupted: A meal missed to the alarm
inn_because_comfortable: A fire lit, and a roof over it
inn_because_equipped: Armed and dressed for the work
inn_contentment_warning: {0} is unhappy ({1}/100). Something is going unmet.
inn_contentment_critical: {0} is wretched ({1}/100) and will walk out in {2} days.
inn_resident_walked_out: {0} left the frith. Their belongings remain at the Frithstone.
inn_tend_hints: Use on a settler: inventory · Shift+Use on a chest: sorting and frith intake · Shift+Use on a follower: come or stay · Ctrl+Use on a resident, then a bed: give them that bed · Ctrl+Use on a tree: keep it standing · Ctrl+Use on a fire, bench or smelter: keep the settlement off it
inn_trait_hardy_desc: Carries a quarter more health than anyone else, and holds on a little longer before falling back.
inn_trait_brave_desc: Fights on at half the health that would send another running, and a threatened frith does not trouble it.
inn_trait_timid_desc: Breaks off much earlier than most, and takes a raid twice as hard.
inn_trait_diligent_desc: Works and swings noticeably faster than the rest.
inn_trait_sluggard_desc: Slower at everything, and rather content about it.
inn_trait_gluttonous_desc: Lives for its meals: a good one lifts it further, a missed one cuts deeper.
inn_trait_sociable_desc: Gets twice as much out of company as anyone else.
inn_trait_solitary_desc: Takes nothing from company and does not miss it; keeps its own counsel and stays the better for it.
inn_panel_stock_desc: What this frith keeps on hand. Residents work towards these figures and stop once they are met, and will not eat a food that is below its target. Targets belong to the frith, not to any one resident. Search for something the Smith knows how to make to give it a target, even before the frith holds any.
inn_panel_stock_empty: Nothing stored and nothing asked for yet. Targets appear here once the frith holds something or a farmer is given a crop to keep.
inn_panel_stock_nomatch: Nothing here matches. Clear the search, or switch back to Everything.
inn_panel_stock_readonly: Only someone who can manage this frith may change its targets.
inn_status_fisher_no_rod: No fishing rod to be had
inn_status_fisher_sail: Sailing out to the fishing ground
inn_status_fisher_no_water: No water deep enough to fish here
inn_status_fisher_alert: Riding it out on the water
inn_status_answering_call: Going out to where it happened
inn_status_sheltering: Keeping out of the way while the frith is broken
inn_line_mood_miserable_1: I am not sure how much more of this I can take.
inn_line_mood_miserable_2: Nobody here seems to notice how bad it has got.
inn_line_mood_miserable_3: Some days I wonder why I stayed at all.
inn_line_mood_miserable_4: I have stopped expecting the day to improve.
inn_line_mood_unhappy_1: It has been a rough stretch, I will say that.
inn_line_mood_unhappy_2: I could do with something going right for once.
inn_line_mood_unhappy_3: I am tired in a way sleep does not fix.
inn_line_mood_unhappy_4: We are managing. Only just, mind you.
inn_line_report_killed_1: Something killed me out there. Somebody had better go and see.
inn_line_report_killed_2: I did not walk back from that ground. Take a spear if you go.
inn_line_report_killed_3: It came at me while I was working. It is still out there.
inn_line_watch_answer_1: Show me where. We will go and stand over it.
inn_line_watch_answer_2: Then it will meet the watch next, not you.
inn_line_mood_neutral_1: Ordinary day. I will take ordinary.
inn_line_mood_neutral_2: Nothing broke, nothing burned. Good enough.
inn_line_mood_neutral_3: The work gets done either way.
inn_line_mood_happy_1: This place is starting to feel like home.
inn_line_mood_happy_2: A calm day is never wasted.
inn_line_mood_happy_3: I have no complaints worth making.
inn_line_mood_happy_4: Good company, decent food. What else is there?
inn_line_mood_veryhappy_1: I would not trade this for a hall in Asgard.
inn_line_mood_veryhappy_2: Everything is where it should be for once.
inn_line_mood_veryhappy_3: I woke up glad to be here. Strange feeling.
inn_line_mood_veryhappy_4: We have built something worth keeping.
inn_line_event_missed_sleep_1: I barely closed my eyes last night.
inn_line_event_missed_sleep_2: Whoever is snoring by the fire owes me a night's rest.
inn_line_event_missed_sleep_3: I am running on nothing but stubbornness today.
inn_line_event_no_bed_1: I would give a great deal for a bed of my own.
inn_line_event_no_bed_2: Sleeping on the floor again. My back has opinions.
inn_line_event_no_bed_3: Is there truly no room for one more bunk?
inn_line_event_bed_in_open_1: A bed under the open sky is a bed full of rain.
inn_line_event_bed_in_open_2: Four walls and a roof. Is that so much to ask?
inn_line_event_bed_in_open_3: I woke with frost in my beard. I would like a house.
inn_line_event_crowded_house_1: Too many of us under one roof. Somebody snores, and I think it is everybody.
inn_line_event_crowded_house_2: I could not turn over last night without turning over a neighbour.
inn_line_event_crowded_house_3: Four to a house is company. More is a herd.
inn_line_event_scattered_workshop_1: One station by the gate, one by the hall. I spend more time walking than working.
inn_line_event_scattered_workshop_2: Put my stations under one roof and I will show you what work looks like.
inn_line_event_scattered_workshop_3: It rained in the soup again. A proper workshop, is that too much to ask?
inn_line_event_good_workshop_1: Everything I need within arm's reach. This is a proper workshop.
inn_line_event_good_workshop_2: A roof over the work and the tools all together. I could get used to this.
inn_line_event_hungry_1: I missed a meal and my stomach has not forgiven me.
inn_line_event_hungry_2: Is anyone actually cooking, or is that just decoration?
inn_line_event_hungry_3: I have eaten better on a hunt in the rain.
inn_line_event_fed_1: A hot meal makes any day better.
inn_line_event_fed_2: Whoever cooked that has my thanks.
inn_line_event_held_1: I keep looking at the treeline. Cannot help it.
inn_line_event_held_2: That was closer than I would like to admit.
inn_line_event_walls_broken_1: They came through the gate. Through it.
inn_line_event_walls_broken_2: I can see daylight where the wall used to be.
inn_line_event_walls_broken_3: Whoever is rebuilding that, I will carry the wood.
inn_line_event_frithstone_struck_1: They struck the Frithstone. The stone itself.
inn_line_event_frithstone_struck_2: If that fire goes out, none of the rest of it means anything.
inn_line_event_lost_friend_1: There is a place at the table nobody sat in tonight.
inn_line_event_lost_friend_2: I keep expecting to hear them come round the corner.
inn_line_event_lost_friend_3: We buried one of our own. I have nothing else to say today.
inn_line_event_watchful_night_1: Stood out there all night. Saw nothing. Good.
inn_line_event_watchful_night_2: No sleep, but no trouble either. I will take that trade.
inn_line_event_unequipped_1: I am not much use with empty hands.
inn_line_event_unequipped_2: Give me something to work with and I will earn my keep.
inn_line_event_unequipped_3: I feel half dressed without a proper tool.
inn_line_event_comfortable_1: A roof and a lit fire. Small things, but they count.
inn_line_event_comfortable_2: Warm in here. I could stay a while.
inn_line_event_new_home_1: Still finding my way around the place.
inn_line_event_new_home_2: New stone, new start. We will see.
inn_line_event_rested_1: Slept like a stone. Do not wake me twice.
inn_line_event_rested_2: A proper night's rest and the world looks different.
inn_line_trait_hardy_1: Takes more than a cold night to slow me down.
inn_line_trait_hardy_2: I have walked off worse than this.
inn_line_trait_brave_1: Let them come. I would rather meet it than wait for it.
inn_line_trait_brave_2: Fear is just something you do afterwards.
inn_line_trait_timid_1: I would rather be behind the wall than in front of it.
inn_line_trait_timid_2: Does anyone else hear that, or is it only me?
inn_line_trait_diligent_1: There is always more to be done before dark.
inn_line_trait_diligent_2: Idle hands make a poor frith.
inn_line_trait_sluggard_1: The work will still be there tomorrow.
inn_line_trait_sluggard_2: No sense hurrying. Nothing is chasing me.
inn_line_trait_gluttonous_1: I have been thinking about supper since breakfast.
inn_line_trait_gluttonous_2: Is that stew? Do not answer if it is not.
inn_line_trait_sociable_1: It is good to hear voices about the place.
inn_line_trait_sociable_2: Stay and talk a while, the work can wait.
inn_line_trait_solitary_1: I do my best thinking with nobody talking at me.
inn_line_trait_solitary_2: Company is fine. In small amounts.
inn_line_role_lumberjack_1: There is always more wood to cut.
inn_line_role_lumberjack_2: That old birch out east is next, I reckon.
inn_line_role_guard_1: Quiet watch. That is how I like them.
inn_line_role_guard_2: I walked the wall twice. Nothing out of place.
inn_line_role_caretaker_1: Someone should really organise that chest.
inn_line_role_caretaker_2: The kiln needs feeding again already.
inn_line_role_miner_1: My arms remember every swing of that pick.
inn_line_role_miner_2: There is good stone in that outcrop yet.
inn_line_role_farmer_1: The soil out there is better than it looks.
inn_line_role_farmer_2: Another few days and those will be ready.
inn_line_role_cook_1: A frith marches on its stomach.
inn_line_role_cook_2: I need more than roots to work with.
inn_line_role_forager_1: The berries are coming in well this season.
inn_line_role_forager_2: I found mushrooms where there were none last week.
inn_line_role_hunter_1: Tracks by the stream. Deer, and recent.
inn_line_role_hunter_2: The forest was unusually quiet this morning.
inn_line_veteran_1: I have done this long enough to do it in my sleep.
inn_line_veteran_2: There is a knack to it. Took me long enough to find.
inn_line_moment_woke_badly_1: That was no kind of night.
inn_line_moment_woke_badly_2: I am awake. That is the most I will promise.
inn_line_moment_woke_well_1: Now that is how a night should go.
inn_line_moment_woke_well_2: Right. Let us get on with it.
inn_line_moment_grave_1: My things. Right where I fell.
inn_line_moment_grave_2: Took some finding, but it is all here.
inn_line_moment_raid_over_1: It is over. Check the walls, someone.
inn_line_moment_raid_over_2: That is enough excitement for one day.
inn_line_moment_rescued_1: I was stuck fast. Do not ask me how.
inn_line_moment_rescued_2: Back on solid ground. That will do.
inn_line_moment_dock_full_1: The caravan's load is still on the dock. We have nowhere to put it - build us a chest.
inn_line_moment_dock_full_2: Goods came in and there they sit. Every chest we have is full.
inn_line_moment_skill_up_1: I am getting the hang of this.
inn_line_moment_skill_up_2: Better than I was last season, at least.
inn_talk_hungry_1_c: I smelled it. Does that count?
inn_talk_hungry_2_a: My belly has been talking louder than I have all day.
inn_talk_hungry_2_b: Mine gave up talking. It only sulks now.
inn_talk_hungry_2_c: Someone ought to tell the cook. Gently.
inn_talk_hungry_3_a: There was nothing in the chests this morning, {0}.
inn_talk_hungry_3_b: There was nothing in them last night either.
inn_talk_hungry_3_c: Then it is a fine tradition we have started.
inn_talk_fed_1_b: It was. I nearly forgave the cook for last week.
inn_talk_fed_2_a: Warm food, and nobody fighting over it.
inn_talk_fed_2_b: Do not say that so loud. You will wake the luck.
inn_talk_slept_badly_1_a: You look the way I feel, {0}.
inn_talk_slept_badly_1_c: I do. Thank you for noticing.
inn_talk_slept_badly_2_a: I did not sleep a wink.
inn_talk_slept_badly_2_b: I know. You talk when you do not sleep.
inn_talk_slept_badly_2_c: Then you did not sleep either, {0}.
inn_talk_no_bed_1_a: I slept against the wall again.
inn_talk_no_bed_1_b: Ask for a bed, {0}. The worst they can say is nothing.
inn_talk_no_bed_1_c: They said nothing last time too.
inn_talk_no_bed_2_b: You and that floor are getting close.
inn_talk_no_bed_2_c: Closer than I would like. It is very hard.
inn_talk_bed_in_open_1_a: It rained on my bed again.
inn_talk_bed_in_open_1_c: Not by choice. Somebody put the bed there.
inn_talk_bed_in_open_2_a: Did you hear the wolves last night?
inn_talk_bed_in_open_2_b: No. There were walls in the way.
inn_talk_bed_in_open_2_c: Lucky. I had a very good view of them.
inn_talk_crowded_house_1_a: How many of us are in that house now?
inn_talk_crowded_house_1_b: Too many to count before I fall asleep, {0}.
inn_talk_crowded_house_2_a: Somebody's elbow was in my ear all night.
inn_talk_crowded_house_2_b: Mine. Sorry. There was nowhere else to put it.
inn_talk_scattered_workshop_1_a: I walked from one end of the village to the other to finish one job.
inn_talk_scattered_workshop_1_c: Because somebody built my stations at both ends of it.
inn_talk_scattered_workshop_2_a: If my stations were in one house I would be done by noon.
inn_talk_scattered_workshop_2_b: And what would you do after noon?
inn_talk_scattered_workshop_2_c: Sit down. Under a roof, ideally.
inn_talk_good_workshop_1_b: Everything in one place, {0}. I am jealous.
inn_talk_held_1_a: When the guard fell, I stood where I work. I did not run.
inn_talk_held_1_b: Then you did more than most, {0}.
inn_talk_held_1_c: My legs did not know how to run. Do not tell anyone.
inn_talk_held_2_b: We held. It did not feel like holding while it went on.
inn_talk_held_2_c: It never does. That is how you know.
inn_talk_walls_broken_1_a: Have you seen the wall by the gate?
inn_talk_walls_broken_1_b: I have seen where it was.
inn_talk_walls_broken_1_c: Then we know what tomorrow is for.
inn_talk_walls_broken_2_b: And went out again with less than they came with.
inn_talk_walls_broken_2_c: Put that way, it sounds nearly good.
inn_talk_stone_struck_1_b: They always go for the heart of a thing.
inn_talk_stone_struck_1_c: Then the heart had better have thick walls.
inn_talk_stone_struck_2_a: If that fire ever goes out...
inn_talk_stone_struck_2_b: It will not. Not while one of us can carry a log to it.
inn_talk_lost_friend_1_a: I keep setting out a bowl too many.
inn_talk_lost_friend_1_b: Leave it out tonight. Nobody will mind.
inn_talk_lost_friend_2_b: Well enough to miss them. Not well enough to say so.
inn_talk_watch_night_1_a: All night on the wall, and not a thing moved.
inn_talk_watch_night_1_b: The best kind of night, then.
inn_talk_watch_night_1_c: Says the one who slept through it.
inn_talk_watch_night_2_a: I saw eyes out there last night.
inn_talk_watch_night_2_c: They thought better of it. Wise eyes.
inn_talk_unequipped_1_a: They expect me to work with bare hands.
inn_talk_unequipped_1_c: I did. The chests did not answer.
inn_talk_unequipped_2_a: Have you seen my tools anywhere?
inn_talk_unequipped_2_c: Then they have walked off on their own. Lucky them.
inn_talk_newcomer_1_a: You are the new one. {0}, is it?
inn_talk_newcomer_1_b: That is me. Still learning which door sticks.
inn_talk_newcomer_1_c: All of them. You will get used to it.
inn_talk_newcomer_2_a: How do you find the place?
inn_talk_newcomer_2_b: Smaller than they said. Warmer than I feared.
inn_talk_newcomer_2_c: That is most places worth staying in.
inn_talk_veteran_1_a: You are holding it like it owes you money.
inn_talk_veteran_1_c: Like it is yours. Loose. Let it do the work.
inn_talk_veteran_2_a: Slower, {0}. You are fighting the work.
inn_talk_veteran_2_c: Took me ten winters to believe it too.
inn_talk_miserable_1_a: I do not know why I stay.
inn_talk_miserable_1_b: Because tomorrow might be better, {0}. That is all any of us has.
inn_talk_miserable_2_b: The roof did not fall in last night.
inn_talk_miserable_2_c: That is a low mark to aim at. But I will take it.
inn_talk_content_1_a: Have you noticed? Nobody has complained all day.
inn_talk_content_1_b: Do not say it out loud. You will spoil it.
inn_talk_content_1_c: Too late. I am happy anyway.
inn_talk_content_2_a: I think this might be home now.
inn_talk_content_2_b: Took you long enough to notice, {0}.
inn_talk_content_2_c: I am slow. But I get there.
inn_talk_glutton_1_a: What do you think is for supper?
inn_talk_glutton_2_a: If I die out there, bury me near the cooking pot.
inn_talk_glutton_2_b: You would only climb out at mealtimes.
inn_talk_timid_1_c: The wind does not usually growl.
inn_talk_timid_2_a: How thick would you say that wall is?
inn_talk_timid_2_c: That is what worries me. Enough is never quite enough.
inn_talk_brave_1_a: If they come tonight, I want to be at the gate.
inn_talk_brave_1_b: If they come tonight, I want to be in bed.
inn_talk_brave_1_c: Then we will both be where we are useful.
inn_talk_brave_2_a: I hear there are trolls past the river.
inn_talk_brave_2_b: And you sound pleased about it.
inn_talk_idler_1_a: Are you working, {0}, or only standing near the work?
inn_talk_idler_1_b: Standing near it is the first step.
inn_talk_idler_1_c: It has been the first step since morning.
inn_talk_idler_2_a: The sun is up and so should you be.
inn_talk_idler_2_b: The sun has no back to ache.
inn_talk_idler_2_c: Neither will you, if you never use it.
inn_talk_loner_1_b: I am sitting. Only further away.
inn_talk_work_lumberjack_1_a: I felled the big one by the ridge.
inn_talk_work_lumberjack_1_b: I heard. The whole valley heard.
inn_talk_work_lumberjack_2_a: My arms still think I am swinging.
inn_talk_work_lumberjack_2_b: Then rest them, {0}. The trees are not going anywhere.
inn_talk_work_lumberjack_2_c: That is exactly the trouble. They never are.
inn_talk_work_guard_1_a: Walked the round three times. Nothing.
inn_talk_work_guard_1_c: Nothing is dull. But yes. Good.
inn_talk_work_guard_2_a: Stay inside the wall after dark, {0}.
inn_talk_work_guard_2_c: It is advice, from someone who has seen what is outside it.
inn_talk_work_caretaker_1_a: Who put the iron in the food chest?
inn_talk_work_caretaker_1_c: It is always not you. One day I will find out who.
inn_talk_work_caretaker_2_a: The smelter ate all the coal again.
inn_talk_work_caretaker_2_c: I do. It is never grateful.
inn_talk_work_farmer_2_a: Rain would do the field good.
inn_talk_work_farmer_2_c: Then we will have to share it badly.
inn_talk_work_cook_1_a: Eat it while it is hot, {0}.
inn_talk_work_cook_1_c: Hot. That is the important part.
inn_talk_work_cook_2_c: Then the forest needs talking to.
inn_talk_work_forager_1_a: Raspberries by the old stones. More than I could carry.
inn_talk_work_forager_1_b: You ate some on the way back.
inn_talk_work_forager_1_c: A forager has to know what is good.
inn_talk_work_forager_2_a: I found a mushroom I have never seen before.
inn_talk_work_forager_2_c: Not yet. I thought you might try it first, {0}.
inn_talk_work_hunter_1_a: Deer by the stream at dawn.
inn_talk_work_hunter_1_c: And they were faster than me today. Not tomorrow.
inn_talk_work_hunter_2_a: Something big crossed the far meadow. Not a deer.
inn_talk_work_hunter_2_c: Not if I see it first.
inn_talk_work_builder_1_a: That roof will stand a hundred winters.
inn_talk_work_builder_1_c: Then it will leak for a hundred winters. Proudly.
inn_talk_work_builder_2_a: Every night something knocks a piece off the wall, and every day I put it back.
inn_talk_work_builder_2_c: Sounds like a war, {0}. A slow one.
inn_talk_work_fisherman_1_c: Only my good knife. A fair trade.
inn_talk_work_fisherman_2_a: Have you ever been out past the point, {0}?
inn_talk_work_fisherman_2_c: More sea. And something under it I do not look at.
inn_talk_weather_1_c: Everything is colder in the mountains. That is what they are for.
inn_talk_weather_2_c: My knee has never once been wrong.
inn_talk_weather_3_b: It is. I keep waiting for the catch.
inn_talk_weather_3_c: That is the catch. You spend it waiting.
inn_talk_founder_1_a: Where does the one who raised the stone go all day?
inn_talk_founder_1_b: Out into the wild. On purpose.
inn_talk_founder_1_c: Brave, or mad. Out there it may be the same thing.
inn_talk_founder_2_a: The stone-raiser came back with half a troll on their back.
inn_talk_founder_2_c: They left the rest as a warning.
inn_talk_lore_1_a: My grandmother said the black ravens carry word to the Allfather.
inn_talk_lore_1_b: Then I hope they have kind things to say about us.
inn_talk_lore_1_c: I leave them scraps, just in case.
inn_talk_lore_2_a: Do you think the Elder still walks the old forest?
inn_talk_lore_2_b: Something does. I do not go and ask its name.
inn_talk_lore_3_a: When I fall, I want it to be somewhere worth a song.
inn_talk_lore_3_b: You fell in the bog last week.
inn_talk_lore_3_c: Nobody needs to sing about that one, {0}.
inn_talk_wild_1_c: They think the same of us, I expect.
inn_talk_wild_2_a: Why do the greydwarves hate us so?
inn_talk_old_home_1_a: Do you ever miss where you came from?
inn_talk_old_home_1_b: Sometimes. Then I remember why I left.
inn_talk_old_home_2_c: And more wolves, I would guess.
inn_talk_hungry_4_a: I dreamed of bread last night.
inn_talk_hungry_4_c: I woke before the first bite. I have not forgiven the morning.
inn_talk_hungry_5_a: Is there anything left in the larder, {0}?
inn_talk_hungry_5_b: A turnip. It looked at me.
inn_talk_hungry_5_c: Then it is ours. Look back at it harder.
inn_talk_fed_3_a: I ate until my belt complained.
inn_talk_slept_badly_3_a: Someone was snoring like a troll with a cold.
inn_talk_slept_badly_3_c: Then I owe myself an apology.
inn_talk_no_bed_3_a: Do you know how many knots there are in a plank floor?
inn_talk_no_bed_3_c: Forty-one. I counted them all night.
inn_talk_held_3_a: My hands have not stopped shaking since.
inn_talk_held_3_b: Mine neither. Hold a cup, {0}. It hides it.
inn_talk_held_3_c: Then fill it. For the hiding.
inn_talk_walls_broken_3_a: I carried stone for that wall all summer.
inn_talk_walls_broken_3_b: Then you know how to carry it again.
inn_talk_walls_broken_3_c: I did not want to know it twice.
inn_talk_stone_struck_3_a: Did you see the marks on the stone?
inn_talk_stone_struck_3_b: I saw. I did not like what they meant.
inn_talk_stone_struck_3_c: They meant someone wanted it dark. They did not get their wish.
inn_talk_lost_friend_4_c: No. I want them to still owe it me.
inn_talk_watch_night_3_a: The stars move slower when you watch them all night.
inn_talk_watch_night_3_c: I named them. Most of them are called Tired.
inn_talk_unequipped_3_a: I tried to fell a tree with a stick today.
inn_talk_unequipped_3_c: The tree won. It did not even notice.
inn_talk_newcomer_3_b: Down the coast. Three days on foot.
inn_talk_newcomer_3_c: And this was the first fire you found? Lucky. Or unlucky.
inn_talk_newcomer_4_a: A word of advice: never sit in the cook's chair.
inn_talk_newcomer_4_c: You will learn. Everyone learns once.
inn_talk_veteran_3_a: Watch what I do with my feet, not my hands.
inn_talk_veteran_3_c: The hands only follow. Always the feet.
inn_talk_miserable_3_a: Everything aches. Even my name aches.
inn_talk_miserable_3_b: Sit with me a while, {0}. Aching is easier in pairs.
inn_talk_miserable_3_c: ...A while. Then I will ache alone again.
inn_talk_content_3_a: I caught myself singing this morning.
inn_talk_content_3_b: I heard. So did the goats.
inn_talk_glutton_3_a: Do you think there is cheese in Valhalla?
inn_talk_glutton_3_b: Is that why you want to go?
inn_talk_glutton_3_c: It is the only reason I would go early.
inn_talk_timid_3_b: It was shut the last four times you asked.
inn_talk_timid_3_c: Then a fifth will not hurt it.
inn_talk_brave_3_a: I went past the marker stones today. Alone.
inn_talk_brave_3_c: To see if I would come back. I did.
inn_talk_idler_3_a: You have been on that same log since noon.
inn_talk_idler_3_b: It is a very comfortable log, {0}.
inn_talk_idler_3_c: It is meant to be split, not sat on.
inn_talk_loner_3_a: Do you not get lonely out there?
inn_talk_loner_3_b: I get quiet. It is not the same, {0}.
inn_talk_loner_3_c: Then I will be quiet with you. For a bit.
inn_talk_work_lumberjack_3_a: Found a beech so old I almost left it standing.
inn_talk_work_lumberjack_3_c: It had a lot of firewood in it. Respect has limits.
inn_talk_work_guard_3_a: My spear arm is going stiff from all this peace.
inn_talk_work_caretaker_3_a: I sorted every chest today. Every one.
inn_talk_work_caretaker_3_c: Because tomorrow someone will open one.
inn_talk_work_farmer_3_a: Something has been digging in the barley.
inn_talk_work_farmer_3_c: Or a neighbour with a boar's manners. I will find out which.
inn_talk_work_cook_3_c: Me, apparently. Do not tell anyone, {0}.
inn_talk_work_forager_3_a: The thistle stung me through two gloves.
inn_talk_work_forager_3_c: Then I cannot pick it at all. The thistle wins either way.
inn_talk_work_hunter_3_a: I lost an arrow in a tree today.
inn_talk_work_hunter_3_c: A tall one. It may keep it. Consider it a gift.
inn_talk_work_builder_3_a: Do you see that beam? Perfectly straight.
inn_talk_work_builder_3_b: It looks a little crooked from here, {0}.
inn_talk_work_fisherman_3_a: A fish took my bait, my hook and very nearly me.
inn_talk_work_fisherman_3_c: It grows every time I tell it. Ask me tomorrow.
inn_talk_weather_4_b: It came down off the mountain hungry.
inn_talk_weather_4_c: Then let it eat somebody further up.
inn_talk_weather_5_a: I think the fog is following me.
inn_talk_weather_5_c: This one does. It is very loyal.
inn_talk_weather_6_c: Thor is busy elsewhere, then. Good. Let him be busy there.
inn_talk_founder_3_a: The stone-raiser gave me a nod this morning.
inn_talk_founder_3_c: A good nod. I will live on it for a week.
inn_talk_founder_4_a: Do you think the one who raised the stone sleeps?
inn_talk_founder_4_b: I have seen them asleep, {0}. In their armour.
inn_talk_founder_5_a: The stone-raiser came home soaked to the bone.
inn_talk_founder_5_c: The swamp. They said nothing. The smell said everything.
inn_talk_lore_4_a: They say the Allfather gave an eye for wisdom.
inn_talk_lore_4_c: Ask me when I have one eye and twice the wit.
inn_talk_lore_5_a: My mother swore the trolls were stone once, and woke angry.
inn_talk_lore_5_c: About being woken. I understand them.
inn_talk_lore_6_a: Is it true the dead fight every day in the great hall?
inn_talk_lore_6_b: Fight all day, feast all night.
inn_talk_lore_6_c: It sounds tiring, {0}. I might ask for a quieter bench.
inn_talk_lore_7_a: They say Yggdrasil's roots run under this very valley.
inn_talk_lore_7_c: I always mind where I dig. Now I mind more.
inn_talk_wild_3_a: A wolf watched me from the ridge all afternoon.
inn_talk_wild_3_c: Just watched. That was the worrying part.
inn_talk_wild_4_a: The swamp has a voice at night, {0}.
inn_talk_old_home_3_a: My father built boats. I build nothing.
inn_talk_old_home_3_b: You built this place with the rest of us, {0}.
inn_talk_old_home_3_c: ...I suppose I carried some of it.
inn_talk_old_home_4_a: Our old village had a bell.
inn_talk_old_home_4_c: Everything. Weddings, raids, lost goats. Mostly the goats.
inn_talk_rested_1_a: I slept like a felled tree.
inn_talk_rested_1_c: A well rested one, at least.
inn_talk_rested_2_a: A whole night, and nothing woke me.
inn_talk_rested_2_c: There was a storm? Then it was a very good night.
inn_talk_comfortable_1_b: And nobody is asking you to do anything.
inn_talk_comfortable_2_a: I could sit by this hearth until spring.
inn_talk_comfortable_2_b: Spring will want its wood split first.
inn_talk_comfortable_2_c: Spring can split its own wood.
inn_talk_shared_meal_2_a: You chew louder than anyone I have ever met.
inn_talk_shared_meal_2_b: You sit closer than anyone I have ever met.
inn_talk_favourite_1_b: I could tell. You were humming into it.
inn_talk_favourite_1_c: A good meal deserves a tune.
inn_talk_favourite_2_a: Did you see what was in the pot, {0}?
inn_talk_favourite_2_b: I did. I saved you some.
inn_talk_favourite_2_c: You are my oldest friend now. I have decided.
inn_talk_diligent_1_a: If we finish the wall today, we can start the roof tomorrow.
inn_talk_diligent_1_c: When it is finished, {0}. When is anything finished?
inn_talk_diligent_2_a: I was up before the cockerel.
inn_talk_diligent_2_b: We do not have a cockerel.
inn_talk_diligent_2_c: Then I was up before the cockerel we will have.
inn_talk_sociable_1_a: Tell me something I do not know about you, {0}.
inn_talk_sociable_2_a: We should have a feast. A proper one.
inn_talk_sociable_2_c: For having nothing else to have a feast for.
inn_talk_sluggard_1_a: Is it time to stop yet?
inn_talk_sluggard_1_c: Then we have been very good at not starting.
inn_talk_sluggard_2_a: I had a plan to work very hard today.
inn_talk_sluggard_2_c: I am still having it. It takes time to have a plan properly.
inn_talk_solitary_1_a: There is a rock by the stream nobody else sits on.
inn_talk_solitary_1_c: There is room for one. That is what makes it a good rock.
inn_talk_solitary_2_a: Do not take it ill if I go quiet, {0}.
inn_talk_solitary_2_c: Exactly. Do not take that ill either.
inn_talk_hardy_1_a: Cut my hand on a nail this morning.
inn_talk_hardy_1_c: No need. It is already tired of bleeding.
inn_talk_hardy_2_a: You would think the cold would get to me.
inn_talk_dreams_1_a: I dreamed I was a raven, flying over the wall.
inn_talk_dreams_1_c: Us. Very small, and very busy.
inn_talk_dreams_2_a: I dreamed the sea came up to the gate, {0}.
inn_talk_dreams_2_c: It knocked. I did not answer. Then I woke.
inn_talk_night_1_b: Nothing that wants us to hear it, {0}.
inn_talk_night_2_a: Look how many stars there are.
inn_talk_night_2_b: Every one a fire somebody else is sitting at.
inn_talk_night_2_c: Then we are in good company.
inn_talk_night_3_c: I meant it would be a good time for a story. But yes, the log as well.
inn_panel_screen_failed: This screen ran into a fault and was closed. The log says what happened.
